name: Slot Reel Resolver
description: Reels, paylines, and a spin whose outcome was decided before it started. The result comes from utility.probability_core FIRST and the reels are then animated to land on it, which is the honest construction: an animation that appears to decide the outcome as it slows is theatre pretending to be chance. Near-misses are therefore an explicit input rather than an emergent property — a designer choosing to show one is making a decision this component will not make silently on their behalf. VIRTUAL CURRENCY ONLY, and the paytable is published the same way a banner's rates are: return-to-player is an output, because a machine that will not state its odds should not be in a game.

inputs.name: reelStrips
inputs.description: Symbols on each reel, in order. Required — the strips are the machine.

inputs.name: paylines
inputs.description: Winning lines across the reels, with their payouts.

inputs.name: nearMissFrequency
inputs.description: How often a losing spin is dressed as a near miss. 0 means never, which is the default because the alternative is a deliberate psychological choice.

inputs.name: spinSeconds
inputs.description: Reel animation length. Presentation only; the result is already known.

outputs.name: returnToPlayer
outputs.description: Published RTP implied by the strips and paytable.

outputs.name: spinning
outputs.description: Whether reels are currently animating a decided result.
